name: Kartu Kredit Danamon American Express Gold

fees.condition: waived by transacting a set amount on the card's anniversary; converting points to airline miles or hotel points needs the Frequent Traveller Option at a further Rp 250.000 a year

welcomeBonus: Danamon has run a bonus of up to 210.000 Membership Rewards points on the Amex Gold charge card. Whether the credit card shares it is not settled here, so nothing is claimed for this entry.
notes: This is the Gold credit card, the Rp 350.000 one. Danamon also issues a Danamon American Express Gold charge card — sometimes called RCP Gold — which carries no preset limit, no minimum payment, and an annual fee of Rp 1.200.000. The two share a name and a points programme but are different products; if the card in hand is the charge card, this entry has the wrong fee.
Every retail purchase earns 1 Membership Rewards point per Rp 2.500, at the same rate everywhere, with no category or foreign-currency bonus.

Insurance premiums, cash advances, money transfers, balance conversions, instalment conversions and cancelled transactions earn nothing. Insurance is matched by category; the rest are matched on the description, so a cash advance or an instalment is only recognised when the description says so.

Converting points to airline miles or hotel points needs the Frequent Traveller Option, a separate subscription of Rp 250.000 a year. The app treats the partners as always available and does not charge the subscription, so a holder without FTO cannot actually transfer at all.

No source could be read directly. Bank Danamon's site, its RIPLAY, americanexpress.com, PinterPoin and IndoMiles are all unreachable from here, so every figure comes from search summaries of those pages rather than the pages themselves. Treat the whole entry as unverified until the RIPLAY is checked.
Not modelled: Priority Pass lounge visits twice a year, domestic lounge access, and the travel insurance cover. None of them pays points.

Six conversions are recorded: 6.000 points for 1.000 KrisFlyer miles, 9.000 for 1.000 Asia Miles, 4.500 for 500 GarudaMiles, 50.000 for 5.000 Enrich miles, 7.000 for 1.250 Hilton Honors points and 6.250 for 990 Marriott Bonvoy points. They were read off the charge card's Frequent Traveller Option screens rather than this card's, and are carried over because the two share one Membership Rewards balance and one subscription. If Danamon converts a credit card's points at a worse rate, this entry is too generous.

At 1 point per Rp 2.500 that makes a KrisFlyer mile Rp 15.000, a GarudaMile or Asia Mile Rp 22.500, an Enrich mile Rp 25.000, a Hilton point Rp 14.000 and a Bonvoy point Rp 15.783. This card earns one rate throughout, so those figures hold for every purchase.

These replace ratios of 8 points a KrisFlyer mile and 12 an Asia Mile, which an earlier version of this entry derived from reported per-mile rupiah figures of Rp 20.000 and Rp 30.000. The derivation was wrong; a KrisFlyer mile costs Rp 15.000, not Rp 20.000.
AirAsia BIG points are the one Frequent Traveller Option partner left without a ratio, so an estimate for them shows nothing.

The four airline conversions are confirmed against the charge card's redemption screens, which show 1.000 KrisFlyer miles for 6.000 points, 500 GarudaMiles for 4.500, 5.000 Enrich miles for 50.000 and 1.000 Asia Miles for 9.000.

Those screens also read "Min: X dan kelipatan: 0": there is a minimum but no step past it, so any number of miles above the minimum converts. The entry records a minimum with a one-mile step, which matters a great deal — a 25.700 point balance makes 4.283 KrisFlyer miles rather than the 4.000 a block-sized step would allow.
The two hotel conversions are confirmed against the cardholder's screens as well: 1.250 Hilton Honors points for 7.000 Membership Rewards and 990 Marriott Bonvoy for 6.250, which is 28:5 and 625:99.

The hotel screens are shaped differently from the airline ones. They ask for a number of loyalty points with the minimum in the field label — "minimal 1.250", "minimal 990" — and carry no "kelipatan" line at all, so only the minimum is stated. Neither hotel unit costs a whole number of points, a Hilton point being 5,6 and a Bonvoy point 6,3131, so the entry steps in the smallest block that is whole on both sides: 5 Hilton points for 28, and 99 Bonvoy for 625. The published minimums are whole numbers of those blocks, 250 and 10 of them, which is what makes the reading hold together.
